summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with a history of liver transplant for HCV cirrhosis, type 2 diabetes, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for acute on chronic kidney injury with creatinine elevated to 3.5 from a baseline of 2.5, in the setting of dehydration and hemoconcentration. She also had a urinary tract infection caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae, which was treated with intravenous then oral antibiotics. During admission, she underwent left eye cataract removal and ECP glaucoma laser procedure, which proceeded without complications. Her kidney function gradually improved with intravenous hydration, and creatinine stabilized at baseline by discharge. She reported resolution of weakness and dehydration symptoms. Social concerns regarding her caregiver were addressed before discharge. She was discharged home with follow-up arranged in transplant, nephrology, and ophthalmology clinics, and instructions to continue oral antibiotics, manage diabetes, and monitor kidney function.
